# ReelBinder

> ReelBinder is a browser-based filmmaking workspace for developing a screenplay into production planning, generated media, an editable cut, and a portable project archive.

ReelBinder keeps screenplay text, coverage, shot planning, media provenance, and edit decisions together. Visitors connect their own supported services; credentials are session-owned and excluded from project archives. The public planning study contains source and planning material only, with separate rights outside the software MIT license.

## Product

- [ReelBinder Studio](https://studio.reelbinder.app/): Use the hosted filmmaking workspace.
- [Planning Study Manifest](https://studio.reelbinder.app/demo/manifest.json): Review the sample description, rights, checksum, and download location.

## Documentation

- [Public Source Repository](https://github.com/kylebrodeur/reelbinder): Curated software source, local setup, architecture, and licensing.
- [Project Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylebrodeur/reelbinder/main/README.md): Product overview and development commands in Markdown.
- [Project Format Contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylebrodeur/reelbinder/main/docs/slate-format-contract.md): Portable archive and interchange contract in Markdown.
- [Credits and Rights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylebrodeur/reelbinder/main/CREDITS.md): Software credits and the separate rights boundary for screenplay and media.

- [WebMCP agent tools](https://docs.reelbinder.app/webmcp/): Connect a desktop MCP client to the browser Studio; the current hosted release exposes 10 tools, while the source/next-release guide documents the 20-tool catalog with typed overhead, frame, cut-sync, frame-history, and still-ingest operations.

## Optional

- [Planning Study Notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylebrodeur/reelbinder/main/public/demo/README.md): Scope and intended use of the source-only sample.
